banner: Synthetic fixtures only — every geometry below is production code exercising production refusals.

intentional_copies_stated: routing.py keeps its own guarded haversine — the router never imports geolock (ADR-0074); packages/geodesy's drift guard pins the semantic cores equal or the suite fails. Duplication with a guard is four-eyes.
census.method: grep -rn 'asin\|6371' --include=*.py packages/ ml/ | excluding geolock (owner), demos, tests, and named-retirement data
census.wave14_miss_stated: gisexport.coverage_gap_layer's closure was missed by the wave-14 census and retired in wave 16 — named, not quietly fixed

coverage_gap_geodesy.basis: geolock.GEODESY_CONTRACT via gisexport.distance_km — the gate computes on the contract it stamps
coverage_gap_geodesy.supersedes: private closure haversine r=6371.0 — the wave-14 census miss, named not hidden (ADR-0077)

drills.name: a polygon ring is left unclosed

result.reason: linear ring at feature 0 is not closed — first position [7.4, 10.5] != last [7.4, 10.56] (RFC 7946 §3.1.6); an unclosed ring is not a polygon

drills.name: a ring arrives with only three positions

result.reason: linear ring at feature 0 has 3 positions — RFC 7946 §3.1.6 requires at least four and a closed ring

drills.name: a LineString carries a single position

result.reason: LineString at feature 0 has one position — a line needs at least two (RFC 7946 §3.1.4)

drills.attack: shape smuggled past the wave-15 range gate
drills.name: a Point wears a MultiPoint's coordinates

result.reason: Point at feature 0 wears [[7.43, 10.53], [7.44, 10.54]] as coordinates — a Point carries exactly one position; a list of positions is a MultiPoint, and a smuggled shape is a refused shape

drills.attack: emptiness instead of an honest null (§3.2)
drills.name: a geometry arrives with empty coordinates

result.reason: geometry 'LineString' at feature 0 has empty or missing coordinates — an empty geometry is a null geometry; use null and say so (RFC 7946 §3.2)

drills.name: a bbox contradicts its own feature

result.reason: bbox at feature 0 does not contain its own geometry — 7.43,10.53 lies outside [7.4, 10.5, 7.41, 10.51]; a bbox that contradicts its positions is a lie with a checksum

drills.attack: beyond elevation the estate has no contract
drills.name: a position carries a fourth element

result.reason: malformed position at feature 0: [7.46, 10.56, 612.0, 1.0] — a position is two or three numbers [lng, lat] or [lng, lat, elevation]; beyond elevation the estate has no contract

result.detail: legal per RFC 7946 §3.2 — counted as null_geometries=1, zero positions checked, absence stated rather than fabricated
allowed per §3.1.1 and disclosed — elevations=1 on the member; beyond elevation the gate refuses (drill 7)

drills.attack: an incomplete census presented as complete
drills.name: the wave-14 census is re-presented as complete

result.detail: the miss is ON this payload — census.wave14_miss_stated names the closure the sweep overlooked; the retired count went 5 to 6 in daylight

honesty.absence_is_not_a_value: empty coordinates are refused; a null geometry is how the RFC says absent
honesty.census_is_data: the wave-14 census missed a sixth private haversine in the gate package itself; the miss is stated on the artifact, not quietly fixed
honesty.guarded_duplication: routing.py's own haversine is intentional and drift-guarded; gisexport's closure was neither — intention is the difference
honesty.shape_before_range_before_stamp: structure is gated before coordinates are ranged before bytes are pinned — an in-range malformed geometry is still malformed
